analysis:
The supplied PR changes are documentation only: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/gptoss-bf16-activations.md, lines 1-22) and one table cell edit in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md line 113. The changed source implementing bf16 activations (SwiGLU clamp dtype) is not in the supplied units, so I could not review the runtime change. Security-relevant claims from the changelog that the next pass should check against the code:
1. GPT-OSS K/V bytes per token halve and slot grants hold about twice as many tokens. This relies on admission and paged storage using the observed native dtypes. If admission still assumed float32, the unified-memory invariant could be violated. That would be an availability risk (T-010, T-029 class, not a confidentiality issue). The docs state admission already uses observed types, but this is unverified here.
2. The gpt-oss-20b 3.5 GiB activation floor was measured on the float32 path and is unchanged. The doc edit discloses this honestly. bf16 activations should reduce rather than raise activation memory, but it is unmeasured. The larger token capacity per grant could raise concurrent KV and activation pressure. The cross-repo coordinator memory-policy agreement (platform structural.go) is also not re-validated.
3. SSD complete-checkpoint namespace changes with layer dtype. Float32-era checkpoints are not restored and simply expire. This is consistent with T-041 (HMAC-keyed names, 30-minute TTL, KEK-wipe purge). The old files remain on disk until TTL or LRU sweep, with no new at-rest exposure kind. Checkpoint identity binding to dtype should be confirmed in the code so that a bf16 and a float32 KV payload can never be cross-restored. AES-GCM AAD and the HMAC tag input should include layer types, which is not visible here.
4. Output is not bit-identical. Consumers cannot cryptographically verify output anyway (T-007). This is not a new threat.
No finding is supported by the supplied evidence. Deeper review is warranted only for the unsupplied code paths, namely the MLX gpt-oss model, KV sizing and checkpoint identity.
